newsitem.title: USA: Massachusetts court dismisses EMLICO complaints.
newsitem.headline: Massachusetts court dismisses EMLICO complaints.

text.p: A Massachusetts court on Wednesday dismissed complaints by reinsurers who were seeking a judicial review of a decision that allowed Electric Mutual Liability Insurance Co (EMLICO) to relocate to Bermuda.
An attorney for one of the reinsurers said he expects the reinsurers will appeal the decision.
EMLICO, General Electric Co 's longtime liability insurer, moved to Bermuda from Massachusetts in June 1995 and then, faced with massive environmental claims, declared insolvency four months later.
EMLICO's reinsurers have claimed that Massachusetts regulators were misled into approving the move so that General Electric could take advantage of the island's more favorable liquidation laws.
General Electric has argued that the reinsurers, including Kemper Reinsurance Co, General Re Corp and Lloyd's of London, were just trying to avoid paying their bills.
In their complaints, the reinsurers asked for judicial review of Massachusetts insurance commissioner Linda Ruthardt's decision allowing the move.
They also sought declaratory judgment concerning the lawfulness of the decision and mandamus relief to require the commissioner to reopen her decision on the move.
Ruthardt and EMLICO claimed that the reinsurers lacked standing to seek a review of the commissioner's decision.
The Massachusetts Superior court ruled in favor of the commissioner and EMLICO, noting that the reinsurers are not policyholders and therefore do not have standing to seek a review.

McCullough said the decision was based on legal technicalities and failed to address the question of whether General Electric, EMLICO's sole policyholder, committed fraud by misleading the insurance commissioner about the move.
"Under Judge King's ruling, the only party who has standing to bring an action against the fraud is the person who committed the fraud," McCullough said.
However, the joint liquidators of EMLICO said they were gratified by the court's decision.

"This decision removes a potential impediment to the implementation of the settlement that EMLICO reached with the Massachusetts Division of Insurance and paves the way for the efficient resolution of EMLICO's liabilities," the joint liquidators said in a statement.
The joint liquidators said the Supreme Court of Bermuda recently rejected a similar challenge made by Kemper Re in Bermuda.
Massachusetts regulators last month reached an agreement with General Electric to oversee the liquidation of EMLICO despite its location in Bermuda.
